style.summary:
style of A: A speaks in short, clipped questions and quick acknowledgements such as I see and Right, keeping the exchange brisk.
style of B: B gives a long, technical, hedged explanation with stammers, then closes with an apologetic I'm afraid that softens the limitation.

A: A's pointed questions keep B answering on A's terms, which gives A control of the direction.
A's brisk acknowledgements prevent B's long explanation from dominating without challenge.
A's terse I see signals comprehension in a way that lets A end points quickly.
B: B's apologetic I'm afraid lets B frame the limitation as regrettable while keeping authority over it.
B's detailed technical register signals expertise that A has to accept.
B's hedging gives B room to qualify any claim A challenges.

A: A's questions are answered with a long technical account, so B controls what each answer contains.
A's short replies are cut through by B's continued explanation, which shows A's brisk style does not limit B.
A's I see only confirms B's points, so B's explanation sets the terms of the exchange.
B: B's expertise is confined to digits and broad phoneme classes, and A's pointed question shows A understands where the method applies.
I'm afraid concedes the point, so the closing of the limitation belongs to the one who raised the question.
B's apology is a hedge that gives A room to press further, so the register does not protect B's authority.

content.summary:
content of A: A focuses on whether the method is used for feature generation, a clarifying question about the scope of the work.
content of B: B supplies the substance, a technical limitation about broad phoneme classes and words that differ by only one phoneme.

A: A's question about feature generation narrows the content to the use that A cares about.
A's observation about the scope of the method identifies what the discussion is really about.
A's question places the burden on B to justify the limitation within a specific use.
B: B's account of single-phoneme differences identifies a concrete limit that the content has to address.
B's claim that broad classes are fine for digits sets the boundaries of where the method is valid.
B's technical detail gives B the substance that A has to build on.

A: B's answer shows the limit applies whatever the use, so A's narrowing does not change the substance B is raising.
A's observation about scope is only a question, and B's limitation is what the discussion actually concerns.
The justification is provided by B's technical account, so the burden does not stay with B alone.
B: B's limit is specific to digits, so A's question about feature generation shows the content depends on where the method is used.
B's claim about digits is a concession that A can use to shrink the scope of the limitation.
A's question can be used to show the substance is about feature generation rather than classification, which makes B's detail less central.

coordination.summary:
coordination of A: A breaks in with a clarifying question while B is still speaking, taking the floor at a turn boundary.
coordination of B: B holds a long turn, then trails off with So, I'm afraid, leaving A to pick up the thread.

A: A's interruption shows A will take the floor when a point needs challenging.
A's question at the turn boundary decides when B's explanation ends.
A's pickup of the thread after B's trail-off gives A the next move.
B: B's long turn holds the floor for most of the exchange, which gives B control over the topic.
B's trailing So, I'm afraid leaves the conversation at B's chosen stopping point.
B's explanation sets the order in which points are discussed.

A: A's interruption is brief and B keeps the floor, so the interruption does not transfer control to A.
A's question at the boundary is answered with more explanation, which shows B determines when the turn ends.
A's pickup is only a clarification that B's trail-off invites, so the next move still comes from B.
B: B's long turn is cut across by A's question, so B's floor is limited.
B's trailing off signals the thought was not finished, which lets A decide where to go next.
B's order of points is a response to A's question about feature generation, so A sets the agenda.

engagement.summary:
engagement of A: A shows engagement by probing the role of the method and asking precise follow-up questions.
engagement of B: B shows engagement through detailed explanation, though with a resigned tone.

A: A's precise follow-up questions show deep interest in the method's application.
A's probing of the role of the method draws out the information that matters.
A's engagement keeps the discussion focused on the points A cares about.
B: B's detailed explanation shows B has invested effort into the limitation.
B's willingness to name the limitation openly reflects an honest engagement with the problem.
B's resigned tone shows B has considered the issue thoroughly.

A: A's questions are short and precise, but B's answers are where the real engagement lies.
The role of the method is something B already explained, so A's probing mainly confirms B's account.
A's focus is narrow, while B's broader explanation addresses the whole problem.
B: B's resigned tone shows B has given up on the point, which weakens B's claim to engagement.
B's honesty about the limit is a concession that A can use to set the agenda.
B's effort is sustained only while A keeps asking, so A's questions drive B's engagement.
